variant.npgsql-default-prepare.note: Npgsql's default Max Auto Prepare=0 (off); the baseline is 20 per D4.

data.note: variants declared linux_only + deferred; set LEDGERBENCH_RUN_VARIANTS to execute a subset.

data.pg_capacity_projection_basis: no scaling applied: pg_cores unchanged at 3, so the projection equals the measured knee
data.projected_knee_basis: PLANNING PROXY, not a measurement: ladder_start_rps 500 x 8 = 4000.0 rps of expected mixed-workload knee. The knee this run actually measures is not known until the first cell's fit, which is what the capacity re-gate (phase `capacity_regate`) tests against

data.note: cross-service response equivalence over every declared endpoint, both SUTs live; this is the validation gate.

data.detail: PostgreSQL ran at 0.1855 of its 3-core budget over the first cell's operating-point windows (dotnet is the binding slot), within the 0.7692 ceiling that leaves 1.3x headroom
data.pg_cores_source: cpuset.cpus.effective, read off the measured windows
data.window_selection: PG UTILIZATION ONLY: confirm-stage windows at each slot's OWN declared confirm rate (`confirm_rates_by_slot`); the common-rate windows the paired verdict uses sit below the operating point and are excluded. This does NOT describe `measured_cache_hit_rate`, which is taken over ALL of the cell's confirm windows (a hit rate is a property of the workload's key draw, not of the rate it was drawn at) -- `cache_hit_rate_source` states its own window count
data.cache_hit_rate_source: MEASURED: redis INFO keyspace deltas over 30 confirm window(s) of headline.mixed.gc-default
data.projection_skipped_because: stage 1's create-only ladder never broke, so its 3715.1 rps is a lower bound on PostgreSQL's ceiling, not a measurement of it

warning_by_slot.java: CI invalid: crossing bracket has 3 rep(s) < min_reps=10. Treat the knee as point-estimate-only: NO inferential knee CI exists at the spec's rep counts (the confirm stage runs at ONE rate per slot, which cannot re-fit a crossing), and the cost verdicts condition on this point estimate. The published cost-vs-rate curve is the mitigation: it shows how the headline would move if the true knee sits elsewhere in the bracket.
